Computers help teens get drugs
By Sue Kramer , Special Writer
Fromhttp://www.zwire.com/site/news.cfm?BRD=1091&dept_id=456010&newsid=5967394&PAG=461&rfi=9

November 6, 2002
TRENTON Computer technology, combined with the ingenuity of today's teens and a wide-open drug market, mean even youngsters under the closest scrutiny can become addicts while their parentless remain clueless.

This is what Terrence P. Farley, director of the Ocean County Narcotics Strike Force, emphasized to a standing-room-only audience at the 12th annual Governor's Alliance Summit Oct. 21.
(MarijuanaNews note: There are wingnuts on all sides of every issue, so it would be pointless to react to every bizarre example of reefer madness, but when you are a prohibitionist you can never be too extreme to be mainstream.

In this case, we have a person in such a significant position of authority to be invited to speak to the Governor's Alliance Summit and whose views are taken so seriously that they are not subject to even the slightest level of fact checking.

In a sane world he would not be allowed to hold any position of authority.)
See
Leading Dutch Anti-Prohibitionists Say, The Quality Of The Drugs-Debate Is Abominable.

" One of the great inventions of all times and yet one of the most dangerous is the computer, " said Mr. Farley, who is also the first assistant Ocean County prosecutor.

" Not only do you have to worry about the perverts on there, hundreds of thousands, there isn't a prosecutor's office in the nation that doesn't have a computer crimes expert. We could shut down all law enforcement activities and do nothing else but stings on the Internet. "

Just last month, he said, an international Internet drug ring was broken up. The group was supplying drugs over the Internet, from country to country openly selling to anyone who accessed the Web site.

" If you have a computer in your home, and you have children, the only place it can't be is someplace in private, " he emphasized. " The computer should be in some place that's a public area of your home that every time anybody walks by they can see that screen. That will save you a lot of aggravation. "

But the Internet isn't the only problem for law enforcement agencies. There's a big " crop " business in this country. It's a crop that's grown, he said, " indoors in New York city, in abandoned factories, in warehouses, in lofts, in 18-wheel trucks, " and that New York City-grown crop alone is selling for $8,000 a pound on the streets.
(MarijuanaNews note: If this were true, it would prove that cannabis prohibition fails even when enforcement levels increase dramatically.)
See
Marijuana Arrests In New York City Continue to Soar. Arrests Will Exceed 60,000 for this Year. Up From Only 720 in 1992!

That crop is not only the most widely available drug in the country, it has also surpassed corn as the number one cash crop in the United States. It's marijuana.

And the U.S.-grown marijuana is being supplemented by " B.C. Bud, " the most potent marijuana on earth. It's a crop that's grown in British Columbia, Canada and then smuggled into the United States. The smugglers, Mr. Farley said, don't have any problems smuggling the illegal crops over the border; it's getting the tractor trailers loaded with $20, $50 and $100 bills back across the border into Canada that's the problem.

" This stuff is so powerful that it is selling in some places in this country, places in California, which has probably the best outdoor grown, and where the outdoor grown sells for $3,500 to $3,700 per pound, B.C. Bud can get $11,000 per pound, " he said.
(MarijuanaNews note: Hardly. First, cannabis is grown indoors everywhere and indoors is the same everywhere. How would the great Canadian indoors be different from New York City indoors? Is there something special in Canadian electricity?

Anyone with any common sense, which would exclude most editors, would recognize the absurdity of this claim.

Second, BC Bud is not particularly admired in California because Northern California has some of the best growers in the world. My sources tell me that it sells for less than $4,000 per pound. The best Humboldt goes for about 50% more than BC Bud.

Third, the quality of cannabis depends on the quality of the seeds, which are available worldwide, and on the quality of the growers, which is a function of experience.)
See
The Drug Czar Harvests BC Bud Propaganda Campaign At Canadian Border. The Jails Are Full, But He Likes That.

This abundance of marijuana and other street drugs has led to a new breed of drug dealer as well. Mr. Farley said no longer do drug dealers specialize in just cocaine, heroin or marijuana.

" We have the first major generation in the history of America of 'poly-drug' users, " he said. " All of the drug dealers now are poly drug sellers. From Jan. 1 to June 30, 2000, marijuana hit the streets so hard (in New York) that 30 former, solely crack dealers were murdered by marijuana dealers to take over their corners because they were so lucrative. Now, wherever you go in New York, you go to the one dealer who's got a supermarket full of anything.
(MarijuanaNews note: Marijuana dealers running off or killing off dear, sweet, peaceful crack dealers? That is a new one.

If this were true and I defy anyone to produce evidence that it is -- it would be an argument against cannabis prohibition. In fact, there is nothing at all new about the polydrug markets. On the contrary, that is a characteristic of contraband markets.

Consequently, the separation of the markets for hard and soft drugs is the foundation of all Dutch drugs policies.)
See
Is the Dutch Coffee Shop System In Danger ? European Elections and the Future of Cannabis Reform. Analysis by Richard Cowan

" Now, the problem is this. Most of the parents you deal with say, 'Oh well, it's only marijuana.' "

The only resemblance to the marijuana of the '60s and '70s, he emphasized, is the shape and color. Back then, it contained 2 percent THC, which is the hallucinogenic component of marijuana. Today's marijuana can contain 20 times that amount.
(MarijuanaNews note: First, there is no data from the 60s on THC. Second, the average potency today is still less than 4% THC. Third, there is no data to support a claim of 40% THC in marijuana. Fourth, saying that today's marijuana can contain any given amount of THC is a comparison of an extreme with an average. That is not a valid comparison. What was the extreme for the 1970s?

InMarijuana Myths, Marijuana Facts, Zimmer and Morgan report one assay from 1975 showing THC at 14%.)
See
Potent Pot Myth Undermined By Report From The Ultimate Authority. Cited By Swedish Prohibitionist Who Don't Seem To Understand. As Usual.

" B.C. Bud, " he said, " is so sophisticated that it is literally spewing liquid. If you were to squeeze that stuff out and put it into a needle and mainline it, you'd be killing yourself. That's how powerful that stuff is today. "
(MarijuanaNews note: Yeah, sure, here in Vancouver we use juicers rather than grinders, and the bodies are blocking the doors at the New Amsterdam.

How incredibly stupid! Everyone associated with this story should be profoundly ashamed of themselves.)
See
Why Do The Best Newspapers In Canada Keep Falling for the DEA/RCMP Party Line?
and
RCMP Annual Report On the " Drug Situation in Canada " Contradicts Staples Of the Prohibitionist Party Line. Exclusive To MarijuanaNews.

The second problem surrounds the way kids today smoke the marijuana. Today, they can pay anywhere up to $25 for an exceptionally large cigar made in Honduras or Nicaragua. These cigars, which are called " blunts " on the street, (not to be confused with the regular cigar that is called a blunt) are so big that they can be hollowed out with a drill bit and then filled with several ounces of this very powerful marijuana.
(MarijuanaNews note: Unless he proposes banning cigars, there is no relevance to cannabis.)

Mr. Farley said it is smoking these blunts that is the cause of roughly 200,000 marijuana overdoses that are seen in emergency rooms each year.
(MarijuanaNews note: Hardly. There were 110,512 emergency room mentions of marijuana in 2001,out of a total of 100 million ER visits. Of those, approximately 25,000 were marijuana-only mentions.

These mentions do not necessarily have anything to do with the cause of the visit, much less indicate that it was the result of an overdose.

In any case, the 25,000 marijuana mentions contrast with roughly 25 million ER visits that were alcohol related.)
See
Cannabis Prohibition Prostitutes Science In New Emergency Dept. Data. Hiding the Truth Behind A Cloud of Lies.

If the blunts are too costly, Mr. Farley said, anyone can walk into a convenience store or head shop and for one or two dollars, buy " commercial blunts, " a pack of two flavored (chocolate, vanilla, brandy, etc.) cellophane wrappers that are meant to be stuffed with marijuana and then smoked.

Kids are so crafty these days parents might not even know if they are smoking marijuana in their rooms or the family car, he continued. This is due to a recent " invention " called " snugglers, " so named because the first ones found by police had Snuggle brand dryer sheets in them.

Snugglers are a simple, homemade " smoke-eating device " that consists of a plastic or glass resealable bottle, such as a soda bottle, with dryer sheets stuffed inside.

" If your child sleeps in the next room or drives your car, they probably can smoke all the dope they want without you knowing it while you're in the next room or while you're using your car right after they did if they use one of these simple devices, " he said. Once the joint is lit, the user can take a drag, blow the smoke into the bottle and immediately seal the bottle. The dryer sheets dissipate the smoke almost instantly.

" The dryer sheets, if used properly, will kill the smoke from a cigarette or from a joint or a blunt. "
(MarijuanaNews note: The only solution is to ban clothes dryers and arrest the Maytag man on conspiracy charges.)

Many parents feel they can avoid drug problems if they remove their children from a public school or inner city atmosphere. Not so, according to Mr. Farley.

" There's absolutely no difference today what community you live in, " he said. " I always tell people when they say, 'I'm sending my child to a private school or a Catholic school,' I say, 'Well, the better the school, the better the drugs. The more money you have the better drugs you can afford.'

 " If any of you are presently spending $48,000 a year to send your kids to NYU (New York University), you have the honor of being in the No. 1 dope-smoking school in America. That $48,000 doesn't count the marijuana, by the way. "

(MarijuanaNews note: How cute! But if that is true, does it show up in NYU's academic standing?)
See
Legalize Marijuana and Improve High-School Academic Performance? Holland Ranks First The US Very Low.
